```
def inbox(patch):
    ai, aj = uppermost(patch) + 1, leftmost(patch) + 1
    bi, bj = lowermost(patch) - 1, rightmost(patch) - 1
    si, sj = min(ai, bi), min(aj, bj)
    ei, ej = max(ai, bi), max(aj, bj)
    vlines = {(i, sj) for i in range(si, ei + 1)} | {(i, ej) for i in range(si, ei + 1)}
    hlines = {(si, j) for j in range(sj, ej + 1)} | {(ei, j) for j in range(sj, ej + 1)}
    return frozenset(vlines | hlines)
```

Hmm wait, inbox returns vlines and hlines but those all are the outline of the inner rectangle. Hmm, actually it returns the full inner rectangle outline only. Wait it's the box of the inner region.

Hmm, but then x8 = backdrop(x7). backdrop computes bounding box indices (all indices in bbox). So x8 = all indices inside the inner rectangle (solid). For the rectangle border with bbox rows3-6 cols2-4, inner region is rows4-5, cols3-3. backdrop gives those indices.

Hmm wait x15 = color(x9) = 4. Hmm.

x10 = remove(x9, x0) - remove the fill object from the partition set. So x0 minus x9 (and minus... well x0 contains all color groups). Actually x9 is a frozenset of cells (with values). Is x9 equal to one of the partition elements? partition groups by value: the color-4 cells are exactly the fill rectangle. x9 is exactly those cells (inner indices are exactly the fill cells). So removing x9 removes the color-4 group.

x11 = remove(x6, x10) - remove x6 (border object) from x10. So x11 = remaining objects = color-0 (background) and color-8 (marker) groups? Also any other colors.

x12 = argmin(x11, size) - smallest object. The marker (single cell 8) is smaller than background. So x12 = the marker object (color 8).

x13 = combine(x12, x6) - union marker and border.

x14 = backdrop(x13) - bounding box of marker+border = all indices from rectangle bbox extended to include marker.

x15 = color(x9) = fill color 4.

x16 = fill(I, 4, x14) - fill entire bbox region with fill color 4.

x17 = color(x6) = border color 1.

x18 = box(x14) - outline of the new bbox.

x19 = fill(x16, 1, x18) - draw border color on the outline.
